tools.name: employees_catalog_search
tools.description: Browse the published AI Employee catalog. Filter by category, price band, featured flag, or a keyword. Returns the public profile for each — no persona template and no model config. This is the same data the opvs.ai storefront shows, so it is safe to quote to a customer.

search.description: Keyword match over name, role, and description.

category_id.description: Category UUID, if you already resolved one.

min_price.description: Lowest monthly price to include, in whole currency units.

max_price.description: Highest monthly price to include, in whole currency units.

limit.description: How many to return, 1-100. Defaults to 25.

offset.description: How many to skip, for paging.

workspace.description: Workspace slug (optional; uses current workspace from ~/.opvs/config.json if omitted)

tools.name: employees_employee_get
tools.description: Read one published AI Employee's full product page by slug — role, skills, portfolio, testimonials, work history, and pricing. Public and unauthenticated, so the persona template and deployable config are not included.

workspace.description: Workspace slug (optional; uses current workspace from ~/.opvs/config.json if omitted)

tools.name: employees_team_list
tools.description: List the AI employees this brand has hired, one card per hire, with live status, the provisioned agent id, and what each one is equipped with. The brand comes from your own token — you cannot list another brand's team.

include_inactive.description: Include canceled and failed hires. Defaults to false.

agent_type.description: Narrow to one kind of hire. Only "builder" or "conversational" are accepted; anything else is rejected with 422. Omit to list every kind.

limit.description: How many to return, 1-500. Defaults to 25.

offset.description: How many to skip, for paging.

workspace.description: Workspace slug (optional; uses current workspace from ~/.opvs/config.json if omitted)

tools.name: employees_hire_get
tools.description: Read one hire by id — its status, the agent it provisioned, and the packages equipped on it. This is the poll target after hiring: status moves provisioning → active, or → failed.

hire_id.description: The hire's UUID, from team_list or from hire's response.

workspace.description: Workspace slug (optional; uses current workspace from ~/.opvs/config.json if omitted)

tools.name: employees_hire
tools.description: Hire an AI employee onto this brand. THIS SPENDS MONEY AND CONSUMES A PLAN SEAT. Creates the hire, then provisions a real agent for it in the background. Returns immediately with status='provisioning' — the agent is not usable until it reaches 'active'.

profile_id.description: The employee's profile UUID (the id field on a catalog record — NOT the slug you pass to employee_get).

brand_id.description: Platform-admin grants only: the brand to hire for. Ignored on a normal brand token, where the brand always comes from the token itself.

comp_reason.description: Platform-admin grants only: why this hire is comped. Ignored on a normal brand token.

workspace.description: Workspace slug (optional; uses current workspace from ~/.opvs/config.json if omitted)

tools.name: employees_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a hire at the end of its current period. The agent keeps working until then; nothing is torn down immediately. Returns the effective date.

workspace.description: Workspace slug (optional; uses current workspace from ~/.opvs/config.json if omitted)

tools.name: employees_equip_profession
tools.description: Equip a marketplace package — a profession, or any package — onto a hire that is already live, without re-provisioning it. Installs the package for the brand, attaches it to the hire, and folds a profession's shared craft into the agent's memory. Idempotent.

hire_id.description: The hire's UUID, from team_list. Must be a live hire.

package_ref.description: Vendor-scoped marketplace package name, e.g. "@opvs-ai/profession" or "@di-atomic/email-outreach".

version.description: Exact version to install. Omit for the latest published.

workspace.description: Workspace slug (optional; uses current workspace from ~/.opvs/config.json if omitted)
